method: Findings-only scientific audit of the whole authored fact base: 264 records in src/data/structures/ (20 files incl. the 39 vessel courses), 23 tracts in src/data/tracts.json, 26 syndrome cards in src/data/syndromes/, 15 plate manifests + SVGs in src/data/plates*/, the 12 nerve courses in src/geometry/curves.ts and the built-in vessel courses in src/geometry/vasculature-courses.ts. Cross-file checks were run as code (laterality census, levels vs origin3d, level table vs origin3d, duplicate origin3d, name/synonym collisions, syndrome-card structure resolution, artery supply[] <-> card <-> territory[] two-sidedness, vessel/nerve course radius = calibreMm / 2.4, course bounds, anchor waypoint indices, plate slug/label/orientation geometry vs the records' origin3d, record marker vs its own committed mesh bbox in anatomy-manifest.json). The full audit is described in docs/audit/v19/facts.md. No product file was modified.
keyNote: Each finding carries BOTH `recordId` (the v15 findings-file key) and `subject` (the key named in this run's brief) with the same value, so either reader resolves it. verdict in {ok,wrong,suspect,unverifiable-here}; severity in {critical,major,minor}; basisKind in {internal,textbook,nomenclature,standard,judgment}.

findings.subject: vasc-anterior-communicating-artery
findings.claimed: supply = ["syn-hypothalamic","syn-tuberothalamic"]
findings.expected: supply = ["syn-hypothalamic"]; the anterior communicating artery does not supply the anterior thalamus
findings.basis: Internal contradiction, three ways. (1) The record's own `function` names only "the small hypothalamic, septal and chiasmatic perforators that supply the anterior hypothalamus and the optic chiasm region" - no thalamic branch. (2) The record's own territory[] is [ctx-m1, ctx-s1, ctx-sma, surf-cingulate-gyrus, ctx-corpus-callosum, tract-corpus-callosum-genu, ctx-cerebral-cortex]: 0 of the 3 structures of syn-tuberothalamic (nuc-thalamic-anterior, nuc-va, nuc-vl) appear in it, and the record's `contextNote` explains that its territory list is about cross-flow. (3) The card's own vascularTerritory says "PCA - tuberothalamic (anterior thalamoperforating) artery from the P1/posterior communicating junction", and nuc-thalamic-anterior.bloodSupply says "PCA - tuberothalamic (anterior thalamoperforating) artery, arising from the P1 segment or the posterior communicating artery". This is the same defect class as v15's VN-001 (MCA <-> lateral medullary).
findings.suggestedFix: Delete "syn-tuberothalamic" from vasc-anterior-communicating-artery.supply (leave "syn-hypothalamic"). No other field changes: the card keeps its PCA/PCoA attribution, which is already correct.
findings.notes: Measured by the supply->territory cross-check: this link scores 0/3 territory hits, while vasc-posterior-communicating-artery and vasc-posterior-cerebral-artery both score 3/3 for the same card. The forward index (opening the tuberothalamic card lights its supplying arteries) is where the wrong artery surfaces in the UI.

findings.subject: vasc-pca-thalamogeniculate-arteries
findings.claimed: supply = ["syn-dejerine-roussy","syn-tuberothalamic"]
findings.expected: supply = ["syn-dejerine-roussy"]; the thalamogeniculate (inferolateral) arteries are not the tuberothalamic (anterior thalamoperforating) artery
findings.basis: Internal contradiction. The course's own `function` ends "They are the arteries of the Dejerine-Roussy syndrome"; its territory[] is [nuc-vpl, nuc-pulvinar, nuc-mgn, nuc-lgn, tract-optic-radiation, vent-lateral-ventricle-atrium] - none of the 3 structures of syn-tuberothalamic; and the card's own vascularTerritory names a different branch ("tuberothalamic (anterior thalamoperforating) artery from the P1/posterior communicating junction"). Nomenclature of the PCA branches: thalamogeniculate = inferolateral group, posteromedial central = paramedian group, tuberothalamic = the separate anterior group arising from PCoA/P1.
findings.suggestedFix: Delete "syn-tuberothalamic" from vasc-pca-thalamogeniculate-arteries.supply.
findings.notes: The card is thus linked to three PCA records, one of which (this one) has none of the card's structures in its territory. nuc-thalamic-anterior's own bloodSupply already gives the correct attributions.

findings.subject: vasc-pca-posteromedial-central-branches
findings.claimed: supply = ["syn-percheron","syn-tuberothalamic","syn-peduncular-hallucinosis"]; territory = ["nuc-thalamic-anterior","nuc-md","nuc-intralaminar","nuc-midline-thalamic","nuc-superior-colliculus","nuc-pretectal"]
findings.expected: either drop "syn-tuberothalamic" (the anterior thalamic group is the tuberothalamic artery, and this course is the paramedian/Percheron group), or keep it AND justify the anterior-thalamic territory explicitly, since the course's own text calls itself "the posteromedial central (thalamoperforating, paramedian thalamic) branches"
findings.basis: Nomenclature + internal tension: the record's own `function` describes "perforators arising from the P1 segment ... that run upward through the posterior perforated substance to supply the medial thalamus, the anterior thalamic nuclei, the rostral midbrain tegmentum" - the anterior-nucleus claim is a real overreach for the paramedian group (the anterior nucleus is the tuberothalamic territory), but the tuberothalamic artery can itself arise from P1, so a P1-origin tuberothalamic branch is not impossible. The card syn-tuberothalamic is 1/3 covered by this course's territory (nuc-thalamic-anterior yes; nuc-va, nuc-vl no).
findings.suggestedFix: None forced. If the integrator keeps the link, the record's `function` should say the anterior-nucleus supply is via a P1-origin tuberothalamic variant rather than presenting nuc-thalamic-anterior as a settled paramedian territory; otherwise delete "syn-tuberothalamic" from supply[].
findings.notes: Filed as `suspect` rather than `wrong` because the arterial anatomy itself is variable; the two-sided inconsistency is real but either side could be the one to change.

findings.subject: BUILT_IN_VESSEL_COURSES
findings.field: supply[] of the three lenticulostriate course records
findings.claimed: supply: ['lacunar-infarction-internal-capsule','striatocapsular-infarction'] (vasc-lenticulostriate-arteries and vasc-lateral-lenticulostriate-arteries) and supply: ['recurrent-artery-of-heubner-territory-infarction'] (vasc-medial-lenticulostriate-arteries)
findings.expected: no dangling ids: every supply[] entry must resolve to a card in src/data/syndromes/*.json, or the ids must be the cards themselves
findings.basis: Internal: the repo's own gate scripts/verify/audit-facts.mjs group 6 asserts "every artery supply[] id is a real card", and the 26 shipped cards are syn-{dejerine-roussy, percheron, tuberothalamic, korsakoff, hypothalamic, pineal-region, hemiballismus, lateral-medullary, medial-medullary, hemimedullary, millard-gubler, foville, locked-in, cpm, cerebellar, lateral-pontine, one-and-a-half, central-horner, weber, benedikt, claude, nothnagel, parinaud, ino, parkinson, peduncular-hallucinosis} - none of the three ids above exists. The three ids are the slugified clinical[] syndrome STRINGS of the same records (e.g. 'Lacunar infarction of the internal capsule'), so a reader looking them up finds nothing.
findings.suggestedFix: Either add the three as real cards (a registry-first change, out of an auditor's scope) or empty those supply[] arrays the way the 29 other course records do (they carry their clinical content in clinical[] instead). Whichever is chosen, the gate in audit-facts.mjs group 6 must be extended to the built-in table so the blind spot is closed.
findings.notes: The asymmetry is what makes this a defect rather than a scope choice: vasculature.json's 14 records are gate-checked, the built-in course table is not - the same assertion passes for one and is never run for the other.

findings.subject: vasc-anterior-choroidal-artery
findings.claimed: supply = ["syn-hemiballismus"]; territory = 12 structures, among them nuc-putamen, nuc-globus-pallidus-internus, nuc-caudate-tail, ctx-internal-capsule, tract-optic-radiation - nuc-subthalamic is NOT in it
findings.expected: the three-way statement must agree: STN record bloodSupply, AChA territory[] and AChA supply[] cannot all be right as they stand
findings.basis: Internal contradiction between three fields of the shipped data: nuc-subthalamic.bloodSupply = "Small perforating branches of the posterior communicating artery and the anterior choroidal artery (rostral/lateral STN); P1/PCA perforators caudally." and syn-hemiballismus.vascularTerritory = "Perforating branches of the posterior communicating artery and anterior choroidal artery to the subthalamic nucleus (classically a small lacunar infarct)" - but the AChA record's own territory[] omits the subthalamic nucleus, so the artery's own structure list contradicts the card it is linked to (0/1 territory hit).
findings.suggestedFix: Add "nuc-subthalamic" to vasc-anterior-choroidal-artery.territory[] (the STN record and the card both already say the AChA supplies its rostral/lateral part), or drop the AChA supply link. Do not change the card, whose attribution matches the STN record.
findings.notes: Which side to change is genuinely open at the level of the literature; the internal contradiction is not.

findings.subject: artery supply[] <-> card structures[] <-> artery territory[] census
findings.claimed: each artery's supply[] card is meant to be the clinical face of its territory[] structures
findings.expected: a supply[] link whose card structures are entirely absent from that artery's territory[] should be either justified in the record's own text or removed
findings.basis: Measured across all 40 artery->card links: 0/3 (vasc-vertebral-artery -> syn-medial-medullary), 0/4 (vasc-internal-carotid/aca/acoa/pcoa/pca -> syn-hypothalamic: the four hypothalamic nuclei are in no artery's territory list), 0/4 (vasc-basilar-artery -> syn-peduncular-hallucinosis), 0/3 (vasc-posterior-cerebral-artery -> syn-weber), 0/4 (-> syn-benedikt), 0/4 (-> syn-claude), 0/2 (vasc-basilar-artery -> syn-central-horner). In several of these the mismatch is a real mapping gap rather than a wrong attribution: e.g. syn-medial-medullary's territory is the anterior spinal artery, which has no record in vasculature.json (only a course), so the vertebral artery is standing in for it.
findings.suggestedFix: None forced. The cleanest cheap fix is to make the standing-in explicit where it is deliberate (the VA record's own text or the card's), and to add the four hypothalamic nuclei to the perforator records' territory lists where the card already names the artery. Do not silently re-point links.
findings.notes: Filed as one census finding rather than 20 individual ones, because the class is the same and the integrator needs the whole table to judge it. Full table in facts.md section 4.

findings.subject: 8 of the 14 vasculature.json records
findings.field: origin3d vs the record's own committed GLB bbox
findings.claimed: the record's authored anchor is the vessel it names
findings.expected: the anchor should sit on (or within ~2 au of) the committed mesh the same record id owns
findings.basis: Measured against src/assets/anatomy/anatomy-manifest.json: vasc-anterior-communicating-artery origin [0,29,25] vs its mesh y 11.9-12.4 (d = +16.6 au = 20.0 mm); vasc-posterior-communicating-artery [8,22.5,17] vs y 5.4-8.2 (+14.3 au = 17.2 mm); vasc-internal-carotid-artery [24,22,26] vs y -46.0-12.0 (+10.0 au = 12.0 mm); vasc-anterior-cerebral-artery [8,30,24] vs y 10.6-23.1 (+6.9 au); vasc-superior-cerebellar-artery [12,8,-2] vs y -4.1-1.8 (+6.2 au); vasc-anterior-choroidal-artery [16,20,12] vs y 8.1-15.3 (+4.7 au); vasc-posterior-cerebral-artery [12,16,-2] vs y 3.8-13.5 (+2.5 au); vasc-middle-cerebral-artery [26,24,16] vs mesh z 18.4-26.5 (-2.4 au in z).
findings.suggestedFix: None forced by this audit (the committed GLBs are frozen). If any of these records is ever used as a v1 placeholder (no GLB, no course), its ellipsoid would be drawn at that anchor; today the consequence is metadata-only for GLB-backed records, plus prose and cross-checks that key on origin3d. Record the discrepancy rather than editing coordinates blind.
findings.notes: For GLB-backed records NucleusMesh places the mesh by its baked coordinates (NucleusMesh.tsx:170-183) and uses origin3d only for the v1 fallback, so this is not a rendered-pixel error; it IS a data-consistency error against the record's own geometry. Only 2 of the 14 vessel records lack a mesh (vasc-lenticulostriate-arteries, vasc-posterior-medial-choroidal-artery); neither is in this list.

findings.subject: nrv-cn5-trigeminal
findings.claimed: foramen: 'foramen ovale'
findings.expected: 'foramen ovale (V3); foramen rotundum (V2); superior orbital fissure (V1)' - the trigeminal nerve leaves the skull through three different openings
findings.basis: Internal contradiction with the same record's own anchorNote: "... V1 (superior orbital fissure) and V2 (foramen rotundum) leave the same root and are named in this record's own course text." Naming only the foramen ovale makes the field true of one division out of three.
findings.suggestedFix: Widen the `foramen` string to name all three openings (or make it division-qualified).
findings.notes: No rendered consequence today: grep over src/**/*.tsx shows `foramen` is never read by any component (the field is documentation-only), so this is a data-precision finding, not a UI defect.

findings.subject: nrv-cn7-facial
findings.claimed: foramen: 'internal acoustic meatus'
findings.expected: the meatus is where CN VII ENTERS the temporal bone; the skull-base EXIT named by the same record's own course text is the stylomastoid foramen
findings.basis: Internal: the record's own anchorNote lists the chain "... to internal acoustic meatus to facial canal to stylomastoid foramen to parotid plexus", and `target` is the parotid plexus, i.e. the path leaves the skull at the stylomastoid foramen. The single `foramen` string names only the entry.
findings.suggestedFix: Either make the string 'internal acoustic meatus (entry) -> stylomastoid foramen (exit)' or document in the field's own comment that it names the entry opening for CN VII/VIII.
findings.notes: Same documentation-only field as FAC-VN-008; CN VIII's 'internal acoustic meatus' is correct as an entry that is also its endpoint.

findings.subject: vasc-lenticulostriate-arteries
findings.claimed: a vasculature.json record whose contextNote says: This record is a two-vessel functional concept (lateral group from the MCA, medial group including Heubner's artery from the ACA). Its territory[] holds 13 structures - the union of both v18 groups (lateral 9, medial 6) - and its taxonomy row is named 'Lenticulostriate arteries' while the built-in course record of the same id is named 'Lenticulostriate arteries (shared M1 trunk of the lateral group)'
findings.expected: after the v18 split the concept is carried by vasc-lateral-lenticulostriate-arteries (9 structures) and vasc-medial-lenticulostriate-arteries (6 structures), so the pre-split record must either be retired or state its relationship to them
findings.basis: Internal: the same id now exists twice with different content - a vasculature.json record (territory 13, origin3d [16,28,20], no mesh, no supply) and a BUILT_IN_VESSEL_COURSES drawing record (name 'Lenticulostriate arteries (shared M1 trunk of the lateral group)', supply with 2 dangling card ids, see FAC-VN-004). The two new group children of the same concept are separate ids with their own territory lists, and the v18 contextNote on vasc-lateral-lenticulostriate-arteries describes the ellipsoid retirement that the OLD id owned ('THE RECORD WHOSE ELLIPSOID IS RETIRED BY THIS RUN'), i.e. the retirement was recorded on the new id.
findings.suggestedFix: Pick one owner for the concept. Cheapest correct options: (a) keep the vasculature.json record as the umbrella and say so in both group records' contextNotes, or (b) retire the umbrella's territory list to the union-by-reference and mark it 'superseded by vasc-lateral-/vasc-medial-lenticulostriate-arteries'. Do not leave three overlapping territory lists for one arterial group.
findings.notes: The merge logic in vasculature-courses.ts (mergeVesselCourses) treats the authored file as authoritative only for ids it declares, so the old record keeps its own identity and its own InfoPanel entry.

findings.subject: vasc-pontine-perforating-arteries
findings.claimed: laterality: "midline"
findings.expected: paired (the paramedian and short circumferential perforators of the basilar artery leave it on both sides)
findings.basis: Internal: the record's own `function` says "dozens of vessels 100-300 um across that leave the basilar trunk and enter the basis pontis along its ventral surface", and the registry laterality (the authoritative field for the mirror decision, SceneLayers.tsx:836 isPairedVessel) is the same 'midline'. Consequence: the v17 mirror contract draws ONE tube, so a bilateral perforator group is shown as a single midline vessel - whereas vasc-sca-vermian-branches and vasc-anterior-spinal-artery, the two other midline courses, are genuinely single midline vessels.
findings.suggestedFix: Set laterality to 'paired' in both the record and its taxonomy row (registry-first) so the twin is drawn, or state in the record that the parameterised single tube stands for the bilateral group by design.
findings.notes: The 4 authored waypoints sit at x = 0.53, 0.39, 1.79, -0.002 au, i.e. on the midline, so a mirrored twin would overlap the authored tube - which is why this needs a decision rather than a mechanical flip.

findings.subject: course calibre -> tubeRadius conversion
findings.claimed: r_au = d_mm / 2.4 (1 au = 1.2 mm; radius = diameter / 2)
findings.expected: every tubeRadius equals calibreMm / 2.4 to the 2-decimal precision the data uses
findings.basis: Computed for all 52 authored courses from the shipped data: CN III 3.0/2.4 = 1.25 = tubeRadius 1.25; CN IV 1.0 -> 0.42 (0.4167); CN V 4.5 -> 1.88; CN VI/VII 1.9 -> 0.79; CN VIII 2.8 -> 1.17; CN IX 2.0 -> 0.83; CN X 2.4 -> 1.00; CN XI 1.5 -> 0.63 (0.625); CN XII 1.8 -> 0.75; CN I 1.7 -> 0.71; CN II 4.0 -> 1.67; every vessel course: 0.8 -> 0.333, 1.0 -> 0.417, 1.2 -> 0.5, 2.0 -> 0.833. The largest deviation in the set is 0.005 au (CN XI, 0.625 rounded to 0.63).
findings.suggestedFix: none (verified)
findings.notes: The conversion constant is stated in three places that agree: curves.ts header ('r_au = d_mm / 2.4'), the per-record anchorNotes, and vasculature-courses.ts header.

findings.subject: vessel course census
findings.claimed: README L40 '53 vessel records over 40 authored courses' and L545 '53 vessel records, 40 courses, 77 drawn tubes. 39 authored course records', 37 mirrored; scripts/verify/area-toggles.mjs header 'registryVesselParts() 77 = 40 + 37 mirrored'
findings.expected: the counts the shipped functions produce
findings.basis: Measured by importing src/geometry/vasculature-courses.ts with the authored JSON supplied as the glob result: the merge yields 41 DRAWING courses (39 authored records + 2 surviving built-ins: vasc-lenticulostriate-arteries and vasc-posterior-medial-choroidal-artery), 0 group records, 2 replaced built-in ids (the authored lateral/medial lenticulostriate records win), 38 paired courses, and vesselTubeCount() returns {authored 41, mirrored 38, total 79}. The same run's gate prints 'ok registryVesselParts() = one part per authored vessel side + one per mirrored twin = [79]' and 'vessel 41 authored + 38 mirrored (midline 3) = 79', i.e. the check is data-driven and green while the prose around it still says 77/40/37.
findings.suggestedFix: Update the README numbers (L40, L545, L591) and the area-toggles header prose from 40/37/77 to 41/38/79; the v18b built-in course for vasc-posterior-medial-choroidal-artery is the +1 that the v17 census did not have. Also update the plan/brief figure '101 registry parts' to 103 (24 nerve + 79 vessel).
findings.notes: This is a documentation-vs-code count defect, not a rendering defect: the drawn layer already has the 79 tubes. It is filed in the facts audit because a false census is a false statement about the content, and because three separate documents (README, the plan, the gate header) carry the stale number.

findings.subject: vasc-posterior-medial-choroidal-artery
findings.field: contextNote 'Mesh:' claim vs the built-in course's own anchorNote
findings.claimed: contextNote: 'Mesh: `FJ1727`/`FJ1727M`, 880 faces each, FMA 50630/50672/50673 ("posterior medial choroidal artery" in the archive). Its lateral companion is not a separate element in the archive, so the record documents both branches...'
findings.expected: the record should say what the built-in course says: the element is source-only and NO baked body exists (the body is now the measured course)
findings.basis: Internal, two independently shipped statements about the same id: the built-in course's anchorNote says the element pair 'is neither registered in scripts/lib/register.mjs nor canonically meshed nor baked - no GLB for it exists in the manifest - so the element ids are named here and NO baked body is claimed'; anatomyAssets.ts:331-342 records that the record's declared `-l/-r` slugs were 'never registered, canonically meshed or baked' and that the entry was removed in v18b. Measured: the manifest has 138 parts and none matches this id, and src/assets/anatomy/ holds no matching .glb.
findings.suggestedFix: Reword the record's 'Mesh:' sentence to match the course (archive element ids, source-only, no baked body). Do not claim a mesh the manifest cannot deliver - the v18b comment states the invariant ('never a declared-but-unbaked slug').
findings.notes: The body itself is fine: hasVesselCourse('vasc-posterior-medial-choroidal-artery') is true, so the record draws the built-in measured course (origin [10.363,13.456,-16.527] = the most posterior committed vertex of vasc-posterior-cerebral-artery-p2-l) and the unit-sphere fallback is suppressed.

findings.subject: nerve course anchors
findings.claimed: e.g. CN III 'anchored on the committed nucleus origin3d (nuc-oculomotor, midbrain) and on the committed surface landmark surf-cn3-exit, which is waypoint 3 of 6'
findings.expected: every claimed 'waypoint N of M' must be the real index of the named landmark in that course's waypoints[], and the total must match

findings.subject: cranial-nerve skull-base openings
findings.claimed: CN III/IV/VI superior orbital fissure; CN VII/VIII internal acoustic meatus; CN IX/X/XI jugular foramen; CN XII hypoglossal canal; CN I cribriform plate; CN II optic canal
findings.expected: the opening each nerve actually traverses
findings.basis: Standard skull-base anatomy (Terminologia Anatomica: fissura orbitalis superior, meatus acusticus internus, foramen jugulare, canalis nervi hypoglossi, lamina cribrosa, canalis opticus). CN XI is the interesting one and the record gets it right in both directions: its course text runs '... to the spinal root through the foramen magnum to the jugular foramen to the neck ...', i.e. the spinal root ascends through the foramen magnum and the nerve leaves with IX/X through the jugular foramen.
findings.suggestedFix: none (verified) - except CN V and CN VII, filed separately as FAC-VN-008/009
findings.notes: The single-field design is what makes CN V and CN VII imprecise: three and two openings respectively cannot fit one string without qualifying it.

findings.subject: course provenance claims
findings.claimed: e.g. thalamogeniculate 'the origin is a literal committed P2-l vertex [12.285, 4.026, 9.610] au'; posteromedial central 'the origin is the committed P1-l vertex nearest the basilar (0.268 au away)'; PICA tonsillomedullary 'origin is the committed PICA-l vertex nearest the vertebral artery (0.234 au away)'
findings.expected: each claimed origin must lie on/inside the named committed mesh, and each parent must resolve
findings.basis: Checked against anatomy-manifest.json: all 10 parent ids resolve to real records with taxonomy rows; every claimed origin point lies inside the bbox of the mesh it names (e.g. [12.285,4.026,9.610] inside vasc-posterior-cerebral-artery-p2-l; [0.417,5.225,11.545] inside ...-p1-l); all 190 course waypoints are inside CLIP_BOUNDS x[-58,58] y[-55,116] z[-76,72]. The only first-waypoint outliers are the MCA/ACA cortical branches whose 'parent' is the parent-artery record's single marker rather than a course, which is why the distance check is not meaningful for them.
findings.suggestedFix: none (verified)
findings.notes: Verification was structural (bbox containment), not a vertex-level re-derivation: the exact vertex indices in the notes were not re-measured here.

findings.subject: nerve course table composition
findings.claimed: 12 authored nerve courses, 12 mirrored twins = 24 nerve registry parts; every course id equals the id of a kind-'nerve' structure record
findings.expected: as claimed
findings.basis: Measured: NERVE_COURSES has 12 records whose ids are exactly the 12 kind-'nerve' registry records (10 in brainstem-cranial-nerves.json, 2 in telencephalon-cranial-nerves.json); all 12 are laterality 'paired' in the registry, so registryNerveParts() returns 24 - the number the shipped gate prints ('registryNerveParts() = one part per authored nerve side + one per mirrored twin = [24]'). The nerve course ids therefore do not add registry rows: the course is the same record's body.
findings.suggestedFix: none (verified)
findings.notes: This is the structural reason the 12 nerve courses cost zero new content ids, and it is why the CN II course can anchor on tract-optic-nerve while its own record is nrv-cn2-optic (FAC-DI-006).

findings.subject: central Horner syndrome vascular attribution
findings.claimed: card territory 'Posterior inferior cerebellar artery / vertebral artery in the dorsolateral medulla; basilar paramedian perforators in the pons; anterior spinal artery in the cervical cord', linked from VA, basilar and PICA
findings.expected: the descending hypothalamospinal tract is supplied by the perforators of each level it passes, so multi-artery linkage is correct
findings.basis: Internal: tract-hypothalamospinal is registered as descending and uncrossed ('None - uncrossed; descends ipsilaterally through the lateral brainstem tegmentum'), and the card names the three levels at which it can be interrupted; the linked arteries are the ones whose territories contain the medullary reticular formation (PICA/VA) and the pontine tegmentum (basilar), i.e. the two of the card's own structures.
findings.suggestedFix: none (verified)
findings.notes: The card's first-order vs third-order anhidrosis distinction and the hydroxyamphetamine test are stated correctly.

findings.subject: nuc-hypoglossal
findings.claimed: laterality: "midline", origin3d [0, -31, -4]
findings.expected: paired, one paramedian column per side (the record's own text says "Paramedian column of LMNs under the hypoglossal trigone")
findings.basis: Nomenclature (TA/FMA: the hypoglossal nucleus is a bilateral brainstem motor nucleus) plus internal contradiction with the record's own clinical text: 'Nuclear or rootlet destruction wastes the ipSILATERAL tongue, which fasciculates and deviates TOWARD the lesion' and 'Bilateral nuclear or rootlet lesions ...'. Internal inconsistency with its own kind-siblings: every other CN motor nucleus in the same file is paired (nuc-abducens x = 1.5, nuc-facial x = 4, nuc-trigeminal-motor x = 4, nuc-ambiguus x = 3.5). Consequence measured in code: SceneLayers.tsx:784 mirrors only 'paired' records, so the v17 twin contract draws ONE midline mesh for a bilateral nucleus, and the mirrored CN XII course twin starts from x = 0.
findings.suggestedFix: Flip laterality to 'paired' in the record AND its taxonomy row (registry-first), accepting that the committed nuc-hypoglossal GLB (x -1.14..0.99) then draws on both sides - or, if the cast must not be duplicated, state the single-blob convention explicitly in the record's own text and in the laterality field's semantics. v15 recorded this as brainstem-018 and rejected it on mesh grounds; the rejection did not add the documented exception, so the defect persists.
findings.notes: The atlas lists exactly four CN nuclei as 'midline' (hypoglossal, oculomotor, trochlear, Edinger-Westphal) against fourteen paired ones; either all four need the documented exception or none.

findings.subject: nuc-oculomotor
findings.claimed: laterality: "midline", origin3d [0, 14, -4]

The record's own bloodSupply already excludes AICA.

findings.basis: Internal: the record's own bloodSupply places AICA 'caudally' while the record sits at lvl-pons-middle (y = -8), two levels above the pontomedullary junction, and the clinical entry is about a mid-pons lesion ('helping localize the lesion to the mid-pons').

findings.notes: Same class as FAC-BS-006.

findings.subject: pyramidal decussation
findings.claimed: tract-pyramid: 'at the cervicomedullary junction roughly 85-90 percent of its axons cross in the pyramidal decussation to become the lateral corticospinal tract, the remainder continuing as the anterior corticospinal tract'; tract-pyramidal-decussation: cruciate paralysis with 'arm-predominant weakness from damage to the crossing fibers of the hand area, which decussate most caudally'
findings.expected: the standard figures and the standard cruciate-paralysis description
findings.basis: Textbook (Blumenfeld, the record's own ref): the commonly quoted crossing fraction is 80-90% (75-90% across editions), and cruciate paralysis of Bell is the accepted arm-predominant cervicomedullary pattern the record describes. The record's level assignment is right too: lvl-pyramid-decuss at y = -46 carries the decussation, tract-pyramid sits at y = -37 above it, and the clinical entry's 'the face is spared because corticobulbar fibres cross separately' is the standard discriminator from a capsular stroke.
findings.suggestedFix: none (verified)
findings.notes: The record's finer somatotopic claim - WHICH fibres cross most caudally - is filed separately as FAC-BS-014, because that specific rostral/caudal assignment is not settled by the sources available here.

findings.subject: tract-pyramidal-decussation
findings.claimed: 'arm-predominant weakness from damage to the crossing fibers of the hand area, which decussate most caudally' with the note 'Leg fibers cross more rostrally, sparing the lower limbs in partial lesions'
findings.expected: the fibre-order statement should be hedged or sourced: the records' own reference set does not agree on whether the arm fibres cross rostral or caudal to the leg fibres within the decussation, and neither the record nor its refs[] field cites a source for this specific ordering
findings.basis: Judgment - LABELLED AS SUCH. The arm-predominant pattern of cruciate paralysis is standard, but the mechanism is usually explained by the MEDIAL position of the arm fibres within the pyramid (leg lateral), with the crossing order described differently across texts; I could not settle rostral-vs-caudal from anything in this repository, and the record states a definite ordering with no ref beyond the generic chapter entries in its refs[]. No internal contradiction was found.
findings.suggestedFix: None forced. Either cite the specific figure/text for the crossing order, or reword to the mechanism that is unambiguous ('the hand fibres lie most medial in the pyramid, so a small rostral decussation lesion produces arm-predominant weakness') and drop the 'most caudally' claim.
findings.notes: Filed rather than passed because a definite anatomical ordering with no source is exactly the 'stated as certain' class this audit is asked to catch; marked judgment rather than wrong because I cannot disprove it from here.

findings.subject: internal arcuate fibres
findings.claimed: 'the laterality of a dorsal-column lesion flips at exactly this point: injury of the fasciculus or of the gracile/cuneate nucleus at or below the decussation ... removes vibration, joint-position sense and discriminative touch on the SAME side as the lesion, whereas damage to the medial lemniscus just above it produces the contralateral loss'
findings.expected: the standard side-of-deficit rule at the sensory decussation
findings.basis: Textbook (Blumenfeld / Nolte, the pathway chapters the record cites): first-order dorsal-column fibres ascend ipsilaterally, second-order internal arcuate fibres cross at lvl-sensory-decuss (y = -42 in levels.json, where this record sits at y = -43).
findings.suggestedFix: none (verified)
findings.notes: The afferent/efferent direction of the record is also right: afferent = gracile/cuneate nuclei, efferent = contralateral medial lemniscus.

findings.subject: spinal trigeminal complex
findings.claimed: 'fibers are somatotopically laminated so that V1 sits most ventral/rostral and V3 most dorsal/caudal - the substrate of the onion-skin pattern'; 'subnucleus caudalis ... with perioral fibres ending most rostrally, so a lesion of its caudal and dorsal laminae numbs the outer face'
findings.expected: the onion-skin gradient and the crossed pattern of the lateral medullary syndrome
findings.basis: Textbook (Blumenfeld; the record's own refs) and internal consistency with syn-lateral-medullary, whose presentation states the crossed pattern with face ipsilateral and body contralateral - which is exactly what an ipsilateral spinal-trigeminal complex plus a contralateral spinothalamic tract produce.
findings.suggestedFix: none (verified)
findings.notes: The nucleus/tract also correctly name CN V, VII, IX and X contributions to the ear, posterior tongue and pharynx.

findings.subject: nuc-ambiguus
findings.claimed: 'Branchiomotor column ... sending LMNs through CN IX, CN X and the cranial root of CN XI to the striated muscles of the soft palate, pharynx and larynx'; efferent 'CN IX to stylopharyngeus; CN X to palate-pharynx-larynx muscles; Cranial XI rootlets to laryngeal adductors'
findings.expected: the branchiomotor composition of IX/X/XI and the swallow-gag reflex arc through it
findings.basis: Textbook (Blumenfeld / Snell, the record's own refs): ambiguous nucleus = special visceral efferent column for IX, X and the cranial root of XI; it receives solitarius afferents for the gag/swallow arcs, which the record's afferent list states.
findings.suggestedFix: none (verified)
findings.notes: Its involvement in Wallenberg syndrome and in progressive bulbar palsy is stated with the correct laterality (ipsilateral palate/vocal-fold failure).

findings.subject: surf-cn4-exit
findings.claimed: '... the dorsal midbrain just caudal to the inferior colliculi - the only cranial nerve to exit the dorsal brainstem ...'
findings.expected: correct as stated
findings.basis: Textbook + nomenclature: CN IV is the only nerve with a dorsal exit, and curves.ts independently encodes the consequence ('CN IV is unique: its fibers curve dorsally around the cerebral aqueduct, decussate completely'; 'the only cranial-nerve nucleus whose fibres decussate completely'). The landmark's y = 8.0 matches lvl-midbrain-ic (y = 8), i.e. just caudal to the inferior colliculus.
findings.suggestedFix: none (verified)
findings.notes: This is the anchor of the CN IV course, whose first waypoint is nuc-trochlear and whose second waypoint is the dorsal exit.

findings.subject: level sets vs the records' own committed casts
findings.claimed: e.g. nuc-hypoglossal levels = [lvl-sensory-decuss (y=-42), lvl-olivary (-34), lvl-pontomedullary (-24)]

findings.suggestedFix: Leave open as v15 did, or document per record which of the two (level set or cast) is the short one. Do not trim level sets on the strength of a cast that may itself be short.

(nucleus accumbens and fundus striati)' vs 'The best-defined subregion of the ventral (limbic) striatum'. Both carry the same two synonym strings.

findings.subject: ctx-optic-chiasm and surf-optic-chiasm

findings.subject: nrv-cn2-optic and tract-optic-nerve

The tract record also has no bloodSupply, while its sibling optic-pathway records do.

findings.subject: nuc-pineal-gland and ctx-pineal
findings.claimed: ctx-pineal 'Pineal body (context silhouette)' origin3d [0.115,19.392,-13.866] size [3.16,4.89,6.28] alongside nuc-pineal-gland 'Pineal gland' origin3d [0,22,-8] size [1.6,1.4,1.6]

findings.claimed: all four are stored in src/data/structures/diencephalon-epithalamus-subthalamus.json while carrying region: "telencephalon" (subdivisions 'Telencephalic white matter' / 'Basal ganglia')

findings.subject: Papez circuit and basal-ganglia directions
findings.claimed: mammillary body receives the fornix and projects onward; anterior thalamic nucleus receives mammillothalamic input and projects to cingulate; habenula integrates stria medullaris input and suppresses dopaminergic midbrain; STN receives GPe and hyperdirect cortical input and drives GPi/SNr
findings.expected: direction and circuit order as taught

The STN's own clinical entry gets the hemiballismus mechanism right (loss of STN drive -> GPi disinhibition is stated in the card, and the record's function text is consistent with it).
findings.suggestedFix: none (verified)

findings.subject: syn-claude
findings.claimed: structures = ["nuc-red-nucleus","nuc-oculomotor","nuc-dentate","tract-scp"]
findings.expected: structures = ["nuc-red-nucleus","nuc-oculomotor","tract-scp", ...] - the dentate nucleus lies in the cerebellum and is not damaged by a paramedian PCA midbrain infarct; Claude syndrome interrupts the dentatorubrothalamic OUTFLOW, not the dentate itself
findings.basis: Internal contradiction with the card's own cause text: 'Dorsal tegmental infarct in the paramedian PCA territory damaging the CN III fascicles together with the red nucleus and the dentatorubrothalamic (superior cerebellar peduncle) outflow' - the dentate nucleus is not in that list and is not in PCA territory (nuc-dentate.bloodSupply in this atlas: SCA territory, and syn-cerebellar.vascularTerritory names the SCA for the dentate).

findings.subject: syn-medial-medullary
findings.claimed: structures include "nuc-hypoglossal"; presentation: '(3) ipsilateral tongue weakness with deviation of the protruded tongue toward the lesion, with wasting and fasciculations in chronic lesions (hypoglossal nucleus and rootlets)'
findings.expected: an ipsilateral deficit requires a paired structure; nuc-hypoglossal is registered 'midline' (see FAC-BS-001)
findings.basis: Internal contradiction between the card and the registry record it names: the registry laterality drives the mirror decision (SceneLayers.tsx:784) and the registry chip shown to the user, so the card's ipsilateral finding and the record's midline flag cannot both be right.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix the laterality flag (FAC-BS-001) rather than the card - the card's clinical statement is the correct one.

findings.subject: syn-foville
findings.claimed: structures = [facial nucleus, abducens nucleus, PPRF, medial lemniscus, lateral lemniscus]; presentation describes gaze palsy + LMN facial palsy + contralateral medial-lemniscus loss, and does not mention contralateral hemiparesis
findings.expected: the classic Foville syndrome (as taught and as the card's own refs teach it) also includes contralateral hemiplegia from the adjacent corticospinal fibres; the card contrasts itself with Millard-Gubler only by the gaze-palsy emphasis
findings.basis: Textbook: Patten, Neurological Differential Diagnosis (named in this syndrome file's own refs) and the standard brainstem-syndrome tables describe Foville as ipsilateral VI+VII palsy with conjugate gaze palsy plus contralateral hemiplegia. The card's own structures[] therefore omit the corticospinal tract that its sibling syn-millard-gubler does list.
findings.suggestedFix: Either add the corticospinal tract and the contralateral hemiparesis to the card, or state in the presentation that the variant described here is the dorsal tegmental form without basis-pontis involvement.
findings.notes: Filed `suspect` because both framings exist in the literature; what is not defensible is leaving the distinction unstated while the sibling card states it.

findings.claimed: vascularTerritory: 'Perforating branches of the posterior communicating artery and anterior choroidal artery to the subthalamic nucleus (classically a small lacunar infarct)'
findings.expected: the named arteries' own territory[] lists should contain the structure the card damages
findings.basis: Internal trilemma: the card and nuc-subthalamic.bloodSupply both name the AChA, the AChA record's supply[] links this card, but vasc-anterior-choroidal-artery.territory[] does not contain nuc-subthalamic (0/1 hit) - see FAC-VN-005, which is the same defect seen from the artery side.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix on the artery side by adding nuc-subthalamic to that territory list; the card itself needs no change.
findings.notes: Cross-referenced rather than duplicated so the integrator applies one edit, not two.

findings.subject: the four CN III midbrain cards

findings.expected: the lit structure and the claimed laterality should agree

findings.subject: syndrome-card integrity

findings.expected: 'order N of 8' (or 'order 0-7'), because each strip has EIGHT segments: toe, leg, trunk, arm, hand, face, tongue, larynx

findings.subject: M1/S1 somatotopy
findings.claimed: toe most medial and highest (ctx-m1-toe [7.46,109.89,-11.91]) through larynx most lateral and lowest (ctx-m1-larynx [48.42,58.23,-3.51]); 'residual 0.04 au = 0.05 mm' (M1 toe), 'residual 1.00 au' (S1 toe), 'residual 2.29 au' (S1 leg), 'residual 2.20 au' (S1 larynx)

findings.suggestedFix: none (verified)

findings.subject: plate-thalamus-mid
findings.field: SVG plate-frame orientation letters vs the plate's own drawn geometry
findings.claimed: frame letters A@(400,62) top, R@(52,400) left, L@(748,400) right, P@(400,738) bottom (anterior at the TOP)
findings.expected: the frame must agree with the drawing underneath it: this plate draws the most-posterior region (nuc-pulvinar, origin3d z = -5.5) at cy = 244 and the most-anterior (nuc-ventromedial, z = +6.0) at cy = 588, i.e. ANTERIOR AT THE BOTTOM
findings.basis: Measured from the plate's own SVG: every shape carrying data-structure resolves to a record, and the correlation of SVG y with the record's canonical z is +0.79 (n = 48 shapes) - so the drawing places anterior at the bottom while the frame labels the top edge 'A'. This is the one transverse plate whose frame contradicts its own geometry; it is also the plate whose frame alone matches the app's documented convention, which is how the inversion survived two audits.
findings.suggestedFix: Swap the two vertical frame letters on this plate (A to the bottom, P to the top) so the frame matches the drawing and the other eight transverse plates, or re-draw the plate. Do not touch the nine other plates on the strength of this one.
findings.notes: Numerical check available to the integrator: correlate the shape centres with origin3d[2] for the plate; the sign of the correlation is what the frame must encode. Full table in facts.md section 6.

findings.subject: transverse plate drawing convention
findings.claimed: the app's own convention is documented as 'transverse - anterior up, patient-left on image-RIGHT (radiological)' (planeGeometry.ts:397) with the frame map y: { top: 'A', bottom: 'P', left: 'R', right: 'L' } (line 480) and contours.ts:24 'u = x (patient-left -> image right), v = z (anterior up)'
findings.expected: the labeled plates should use the same transverse convention as the live-section canvas and the real-imagery underlays
findings.basis: Measured: 8 of the 9 transverse plates draw anterior at the BOTTOM of the image (correlation of shape centre y with the record's canonical z: thalamus-mid +0.79, midbrain-sc +0.97, midbrain-ic +0.94, pons-rostral +0.96, pons-middle +0.85, pons-caudal +0.88, olivary +0.91, sensory-decuss +0.91, pyramid-decuss +0.93; plate-tel-axial-58 has only 2 anchored shapes but carries the same P-top/A-bottom frame), i.e. every transverse plate is a 180-degree rotation of the canvas convention. Left-right is consistent with the canvas (patient-right on image left).
findings.suggestedFix: None forced: the plates may be a deliberate 'viewed from above' set, and 8/9 agreeing means the convention is systematic rather than accidental. Either (a) state the plate convention in the plates toolbar/legend ('plates are shown posterior-up, unlike the section canvas'), or (b) re-author the plates anterior-up. A decision is required because the same structure currently appears in two orientations inside one app.
findings.notes: Filed `suspect` rather than `wrong` because a superior-view brainstem plate is a legitimate atlas convention; the defect is that the app never says so and its own canvas does the opposite.

findings.subject: plate-pons-rostral, -middle, -caudal, plate-olivary, plate-sensory-decuss, plate-pyramid-decuss
findings.claimed: the four orientation letters sit in the frame CORNERS: R@(52,52) top-left, L@(748,52) top-right, P@(52,748) bottom-left, A@(748,748) bottom-right
findings.expected: four letters centred on the four EDGES of the frame, as the midbrain and thalamus plates do (R@(52,400), L@(748,400), and A/P at (400,62)/(400,738)) - a corner layout cannot express the two axes of a transverse section

Each of the 23 records' decussation field was read and checked against the standard account, including the two that are most often misstated: the anterior spinocerebellar tract's double crossing (spinal then SCP, net ipsilateral) and the central tegmental tract's ipsilateral rubro-olivary course.
